market_context.summary: Friday 2026-08-28 repriced the Fed. Chair Kevin Warsh, in his first Jackson Hole appearance as chair, said underlying inflation trends have not improved and that the Fed will 'have work to do' — and the market-implied probability of a HIKE at the September 15-16 FOMC went from ~35% to 55.7-60%, with a cut at effectively zero. The 2-year jumped 12bp to 4.35% against a 5.6bp move in the 10-year: a bear flattener, front end doing the work. The index barely moved (S&P -0.25%) while the rate-sensitive complex was hit hard — Russell 2000 -1.39%, utilities, telecom and REITs the laggards, gold -2.88% to $4,529.90, GLD closing below its 200-day for the first time in this cycle, uranium (CCJ -5.94%) and semis (NVDA -4.58%, SMH -3.47%) sold, with large-cap tech the only leadership. That ordering — highest multiple falls most — is a duration repricing, not an AI-demand signal. The ECB signalled the same way, so this is a global hawkish tilt. Separately and largely unpriced: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed six months into the Iran conflict, countries in conflict now account for over 43% of world oil supply, and Russia's gasoline/diesel export bans plus drone strikes that cut its refinery throughput below 60% of capacity have pushed the diesel crack to a record $102/bbl. Friday's payroll print on 09-04 is the week's fulcrum — it decides whether a September hike is deliverable.

entry.condition: CONTINUING POSITION filled at 93.00 on 2026-08-22. Do NOT add at 99.71 — the stock is 0.4% from its 250-day high and 42% above the highest published analyst target.

exit.scale_plan: Trim HALF at the Monday 2026-08-31 open near 99-100. Trail the remainder against the raised 92.00 stop toward 108.

catalyst.event: Russian gasoline export ban runs to end-2026 and the diesel ban to 2027-01-31, with Russian refinery throughput under 60% of capacity after 21 August drone strikes; EIA inventories Wed Sep 2 10:30 ET
catalyst.action: Trim half at the open Monday, then hold the rest against a 92.00 stop through the EIA print.

recommendations.thesis: The refining shock is real and dated: a record 21 Ukrainian drone strikes in August cut Russian refinery throughput below 4 MMb/d, under 60% of capacity and the lowest in over 20 years, removing ~1.1 mmb/d of refined product from world markets and pushing the diesel crack to a record $102/bbl. HF Sinclair is capturing it — Q2 revenue $10.39B beat consensus by 38.55%, adjusted EPS $5.31 vs $4.60, refining EBITDA $1.02B on a 57% jump in gross margin to $25.95 per produced barrel. Director Franklin Myers bought 15,000 shares at $85.30 on 2026-08-11.
recommendations.key_risk: DINO at 99.71 trades roughly 42% above the highest published analyst target of $70 (UBS), with the consensus quoted between $53.71 and $76.29 and Raymond James at $60. Record crack spreads mean-revert, and a Hormuz reopening or a Russian refining recovery would compress the entire thesis quickly. This is a position to protect, not to extend.
recommendations.counter_argument: Sell-side targets lag commodity cycles badly and none of them modelled a $102 diesel crack, so the gap to target may say more about stale models than about DINO. Fair — but that is the argument every holder of a parabolic commodity name makes at the high, and it is not a reason to hold full size 0.4% below a 250-day high.

recommendations.counter_argument: A tighter stop on a name that has already stopped out three times invites a fourth stop-out, and the honest alternative is to close DHT now rather than dress up a fourth attempt. That is a defensible reading; the position is held only because both legs are green and the supply catalyst is still live.

catalyst.event: New CEO Steve Cahillane's turnaround: a $600M brand investment push he calls mostly undeployed dry powder, and a separation into Global Taste Elevation and North American grocery that is paused rather than cancelled
catalyst.action: Accumulate on weakness toward 23.50 in thirds over the next two quarters. There is no dated catalyst and no need to hurry.

recommendations.thesis: Kraft Heinz guides FY2026 adjusted EPS to $2.03-2.09, so at 25.70 it trades at about 12.5x with a $1.60 dividend yielding 6.2%, and management RAISED the organic sales outlook at Q2 from a 1.5-3.5% decline to a 0.5-2.0% decline. Steve Cahillane, the former Kellanova CEO who took the chair in January 2026, bought 213,106 shares in the open market at a weighted average $23.4616 on 2026-05-12 — roughly $5.0M of his own money four months into the job, against just $0.77M of insider selling across the whole six-month window. He paused the announced two-way split to fix the business first and is deploying a $600M brand investment he describes as largely untouched.
recommendations.key_risk: Organic sales are still shrinking, just less quickly, and the dividend has not been raised in seven years at a 78% payout ratio — so the 6.2% yield is a symptom of low expectations, not a margin of safety. Packaged food faces genuine secular pressure from GLP-1 demand effects and private label, and a paused split can quietly become a cancelled one. The invalidation is concrete: two consecutive quarters of organic sales declining faster than 2.5%, or any cut to the $1.60 dividend.
recommendations.counter_argument: This is the classic value trap shape — cheap multiple, high yield, declining volumes, activist-free — and Kraft Heinz has burned turnaround buyers repeatedly since the 2019 writedown. A single CEO purchase, however large, is one person's opinion, and the six-month file shows only one distinct buyer, not the multi-buyer cluster that carries real predictive weight.

data_quality_notes:
Research phase completed and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block — nothing here is truncated. 15 candidates captured, 14 published, 1 demoted to the watchlist on the reward-to-risk floor.

HOW BELOW-FLOOR IDEAS WERE HANDLED, because two of them were. Research's own self-audit flagged that LULU (2.17) and MDT (2.08) fall below the 2.5 long-term floor, and said so rather than nudging the bear case up to make them pass. Synthesis recomputed both independently from entry, target and bear-case price and confirms those numbers. They are split on one line: does today's action ADD risk or REMOVE it? MDT asks the reader to buy a third of a new position, so it is demoted to the watchlist — with the Sep 1 earnings timing instruction preserved there, because that instruction reduces risk regardless of the ratio. LULU asks the holder to SELL half before Thursday's print, so it is published: a ratio floor screens new risk and cannot evaluate an instruction to cut. The 2.17 is stated in the idea itself, and its entry condition forbids adding above 118. Nobody is being asked to buy LULU at that ratio.

THREE RECOMMENDATIONS HAVE NO REWARD-TO-RISK BY CONSTRUCTION and they are the most valuable things in this report. Ranks 1, 2 and 3 — the /MBTU6 cover, the TJX close and the TLT close — are exits. An exit has no target and therefore no ratio; risk_reward is null, honestly, not as an omission. This matters because on both 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-29 the mechanical validation demoted exactly these instructions to the watchlist for failing a ratio check they cannot pass, so the reader never saw them, and the /MBTU6 short is now ~22% offside eleven days past its own stop. Two of today's three closes are positions whose stated stops were breached and never executed. Do not let a ratio floor suppress a cover, a close or a trim.

RANKING, AND WHY IT LOOKS ODD. Ranking is conviction first, then recomputed reward-to-risk, per config/strategy.md. That mechanically puts XLE (29.0) and DINO (15.0) at the top of the conviction-3 block. Those ratios are not fitted targets — they are the opposite, and they are close to meaningless. Both are existing profitable positions where today's action is to raise a protective stop to just below the original entry, so the denominator collapses toward zero. Read them as 'risk on a winner has been cut to almost nothing', not as attractive entries. Neither is a buy at the current price and each says so in its entry condition. Note also that PFE, CCJ and LCII appear here at 5.55, 2.67 and 4.40 rather than the 61, 26.7 and 22 recorded in the research notes: those were computed against stops, and the long-term floor is measured against a stated bear-case price. Recomputing them correctly is what dropped them to sane numbers.

NO CLUSTERING AT THE FLOOR — the fitted-target signature is absent. The surviving ratios spread across 2.17, 2.24, 2.56, 2.67, 2.81, 3.00, 4.25, 4.40, 5.55, 15.0 and 29.0. Nothing sits suspiciously just above its bar, and the one idea closest to a floor (LULU at 2.17) is below it and disclosed.

THE DAY'S DOMINANT FACT is Warsh's Jackson Hole speech moving the September FOMC from ~35% to 55.7-60% odds of a HIKE, with a cut at effectively zero. That is why TLT is closed rather than held to its 86.20 target, and why the GLD, EEM and NKE limit orders are cancelled — in each case the premise inverted, not just the price. Three ideas (HOG, LCII, NKE) all depend on rate-sensitive big-ticket financed demand and are all on the wrong side of that print. That is exactly at the 3-idea correlation cap and it is the concentration to watch; HOG is a limit 6.8% below market that may never fill. Long energy is also exactly at the cap (XLE, DINO, DHT), which is why MTDR was rejected today despite a 7-buyer insider cluster.

ALL THREE NEW IDEAS ARE LIMITS BELOW MARKET AND NONE MAY FILL. KHC at 23.50 is 8.6% below Friday's close, HOG at 26.20 is 6.8% below, AMR at 200.00 is 11.6% below. That is deliberate: at Friday's closing prices none of the three clears its floor (AMR at 226.23 gives 0.62, HOG at 28.10 gives 1.50). A day that generates three good theses and zero fills is a correct outcome, not a failure.

PRICES AND SOURCES THAT FAILED. This is a Sunday run: US equities and futures are closed and every single-name price in this report is the Friday 2026-08-28 close from finnhub, re-fetched during synthesis and confirmed unchanged — a closed market, not stale data. BTC is live from CoinGecko at 78,689. What could NOT be fetched: Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every symbol all morning, so there is no independently verified index, VIX, dollar, gold or crude print — the levels in market_context come from cited web sources and vix is null rather than guessed. Kalshi price fields returned null on both the list and single-market endpoints and market_data.py events returned count 0 for every macro keyword, so no event contract was captured; guessing a cents price would have been fabrication. sec.gov EDGAR primary documents returned HTTP 403 on the LULU 13D/A and the KHC Q2 exhibit, businesswire timed out on the KHC release, and direct cnbc.com fetches returned 403 — CNBC figures come from search extracts rather than fetched pages.

COVERAGE GAPS. No event contract (unpriceable, above). No new crypto position despite crypto being the only live venue on a Sunday — BTC/ETH/SOL/DOGE/LINK/AVAX all moved +0.2% to +1.6% in a tight cluster, so there is no dispersion to trade, and the ETH staking-yield thesis carried over from 2026-08-29 was falsified on the arithmetic: ~2.0-2.6% net staking yield against 3.63% fed funds and a 4.35% 2-year means staked ETH yields 100-235bp LESS than risk-free cash with all of ETH's volatility. No directional futures idea beyond the cover: a coin-flip FOMC already priced as a coin flip is not an edge. Zero insider buying across 19 semis and semicap names screened, two days after NVDA's +8.7%/-4.6% round trip and three days before AVGO reports — noted, not traded. Not reached at all: REITs, utilities beyond the existing CEG/VST orders, international ADRs, and anything under $500M market cap.

HORIZON SKEW, unforced. Six swing, seven long-term, one intraday — and the single intraday idea is a futures cover, not a day trade. On a Sunday with no live equity session that is the honest shape; no idea was added or dropped to balance it.

SIZING NOTE. NKE's conviction was cut from 3 to 2 by research on repetition grounds — it is the third pitch in ten days with no new evidence — so its position_size_pct is set to the 1% lottery-ticket cap per config/strategy.md, below the 2% it carried. That is a cap on adding, not an instruction to sell; the recommendation remains hold-and-do-not-add. AMR is conviction 2 at 1% for the same reason. The two closes and the /MBTU6 cover carry position_size_pct 0 because they are exits.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. 0 of 9 closed trades have hit target, average -3.3%. That is under the ~15-trade threshold where the sample means anything, so it is noise rather than a signal to over-fit — but the recurring failure mode in it is visible and is not noise: five recent stop-outs, three of them DHT re-entries on consecutive days, plus two live positions carrying stops that were breached and ignored. Today's report is disproportionately risk-management for that reason. Validation demoted 6 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 8 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.
